decisions.name: Example 4.6.5, Set_mono as a locally cartesian closed category without products
decisions.reason: This is a boundary illustration about slices of monomorphisms without products. It is not used by any retained theorem or example on this pair.
decisions.evidence: The live MA-14 route already homes local cartesian closure through `def-locally-cartesian-closed-category` and items 20-24 on the A page, while the current B page keeps only six examples and none needs a productless locally cartesian closed witness. `research/plan-category-theory-track.md:2589-2600` treats the retained LCC block as slice inheritance, terminal-object reduction, finite-limit consequences, the pullback-functor characterization, and Set. No current manifest item cites Example 4.6.5, so this boundary example remains a genuine out-of-scope exclusion on Monday, August 31, 2026.

decisions.name: Example 4.4.14, Top is not cartesian closed but convenient categories of spaces are
decisions.reason: Riehl uses this as a motivation for convenient categories of spaces. The pair already has a simpler A-page counterexample to closedness, and a direct Top proof here would need additional function-space or quotient-space machinery not otherwise used on the page.
decisions.evidence: MA-14 already supplies `cex-a-monoidal-category-need-not-be-closed` as its A-page witness that closedness is not automatic, and the current B page does not home any topological-space example. Adding Riehl Example 4.4.14 would require extra function-space or quotient-space machinery absent from the live manifest and unnecessary for any retained item. The out-of-scope decision therefore stands on the current August 31, 2026 bytes.

decisions.name: 7.9 Internal Homs in module categories
decisions.reason: This is the module-category notion of internal Hom, not the closed-monoidal notion this page is building. I read it precisely to avoid mining EGNO for the wrong definition.
decisions.evidence: Kelly and Riehl are the live positive carriers for closed and biclosed monoidal categories on MA-14. EGNO 7.9 concerns internal Homs in module categories, which is a different notion from right adjoints to tensor in a monoidal category, and the batch notes keep that section only as a trap against importing the wrong definition. No retained MA-14 theorem or example needs EGNO 7.9 as a positive scaffold result, so this out-of-scope decision stands.

decisions.name: The formal-power-series half of the theorem on polynomial and power-series extensions

decisions.name: Remark 1.3.5, the mnemonic exact triangle
decisions.reason: This is the exact-triangle mnemonic that motivates the later triangulated-category formalism. The present page works entirely at the chain and homology level and does not yet introduce distinguished triangles as independent objects.
decisions.evidence: HA-4's live manifest stops at chain- and cochain-level long exact sequences, the cone long exact sequence, and the relative-homology sequence. Weibel's exact-triangle mnemonic is explicitly triangulated-category motivation, and `research/plan-homological-algebra-track.md` later homes that subject on `triangulated-categories`. Because no current HA-4 item treats distinguished triangles as independent objects, this deferment stands.

decisions.name: Exercise 6.3.27(c), every presheaf category is a topos
decisions.reason: The page deliberately stops after subobject classifiers. Turning the whole presheaf-category conclusion into a topos theorem would cross the explicit boundary against elementary-topos development.
decisions.evidence: MA-14 ends with `def-subobject-classifier`, `thm-a-subobject-classifier-represents-the-subobject-functor`, `thm-the-two-element-set-is-a-subobject-classifier-for-sets`, and `rem-what-is-not-developed-here`. The live page deliberately stops before elementary-topos axioms, and a literal search of `research/plan-spec.json` plus the current MA track on Monday, August 31, 2026 finds no page tasked with proving the full theorem that every presheaf category is a topos. Since the retained presheaf-classifier example does not need that stronger conclusion, this out-of-scope boundary stands.
